The sky brightness is astronomical twilight, the sky is clear, and I'm an ordinary adult with normal unaided eyesight who knows roughly where to look.

Yes — very likely.

At 9.1° altitude, the Moon is low but definitely above a flat, unobstructed horizon. With 91% illumination it will be extremely bright, easily visible to normal unaided eyesight even during astronomical twilight. A clear sky helps substantially.

Look roughly east-southeast (azimuth about 109°, measured clockwise from north). Because it is only about a fist-width above the horizon at arm’s length, buildings, hills, haze, or local light pollution near the horizon could hide it. But if you have a clear view in that direction, it should be obvious.
